utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. We should continue with the hearing of expert witness Dr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: May I proceed, Mr. President? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, we only have 30 minutes, so we are going to have to rattle through this. The first thing I'd like you to do is if you could turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 41, which is the last exhibit in the bundle of documents.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What is that document, Dr. Donia?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the decision of the assembly of the Serbian people of Prijedor municipality to join the Autonomous Region of the Bosnian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And just to be absolutely specific, this decision is for the Serbian territories in the Prijedor municipality to join?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Undefined but nevertheless Serbian territories of the Prijedor municipality joined by this decision to the ARK.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Do we know whether the non-Serb delegates to the Municipal Assembly in Prijedor participated in making this decision?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were not members of the Serbian assembly, so it would be inconceivable that they would have participated.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So this was a unilateral decision of the Serbian assembly to join the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could now go back, please, to Prosecutor's Exhibit 12, which are the Prijedor SDS minutes, and if you could go, please, to the meeting of the 31st of January of 1992, which takes place 14 days after the proclamation or the decision on Serbian territories joining the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina. Could you highlight the important elements of this meeting, please, Dr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document is entitled, "Minutes of the SDS municipal board meeting 31 January 1992." It was presided over by party president Simo Miskovic. It is the first of two meetings in which the reports are given about Bosnian Serb meetings outside of Prijedor. In this case, a report by President Miskovic, halfway down the page, one sees this entry: Miskovic gave a briefing on the session of the Bosnian Krajina -- Bosanska Krajina assembly, and then lists several items: Delegation in Belgrade visiting Milosevic three options on the fate of the Serbian people were stated, and skipping to the Statute of Krajina was adopted at the last session of the Bosanska Krajina assembly. At the bottom of this page, under Srdic, "the most important thing to be done in Prijedor is to add Prijedor to Bosnian Krajina." This suggests that the decision of the Serbian assembly to join the Bosnian Krajina was not sufficient in the minds of the party -- one of the party leaders, anyway, that the entire Prijedor municipality needed to come under the jurisdiction of the Bosnian Krajina. On the following page, Mr. Timarac, third line down: "For us, the month of February is crucial if the referendum is held, the transformation is to begin immediately." The referendum here is the scheduled referendum of 29 March -- 29 February and 1 March regarding the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which by this time was scheduled, and the transformation, as will subsequently be seen in these documents, comes to refer to a transformation of who holds the power in Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you have nothing further to add on that set of minutes, Dr. Donia, if we could now go to the meeting of the 17th of February of 1992, which Your Honours will find on page 457, the ERN number is at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a meeting of the SDS Prijedor municipal board of 17 February 1992. The agenda item, sole agenda item, is the briefing on the meeting of the Main Board and Serbian Assembly. And in the next line one sees Simo Miskovic, the president of the SDS board, gave a briefing on the meeting held in Sarajevo. Mr. Karadzic, president of the SDS BH was the main speaker. It was an act of secession of the BH on the part of the SDA. He's referring here to the impending referendum on independence. "In that respect, we are forced to create national communities on ethnic territories." Down two paragraphs: "In the Republic, there will be a maximum strengthening of authority in the regions economically and politically, and the activities in the region of Bosnian Krajina are geared towards that. After the situation in the country calmed down and the preconditions are there, the will of the people will bring about the unification of all Serb territories and communities." So this positions the Bosnian Krajina as a transitional organ of government which would ultimately be dissolved, as in fact it was in September of 1992. Continuing with this summary of the report of Dr. Karadzic's remarks, down three sentences: "Serbs shall not participate in any way in the referendum conducted by the SDA. In view of that, it is necessary to activate the second stage of the position stated by the SDS BH Main Board." This refers to the second stage of the instructions of 19 December 1991. "It is absolutely necessary to cover the territory and the population, Serbs, by activists and representatives. Each should secure his own area."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, a couple of questions. You stated that the stated position was that the government of the Bosnian Krajina would be a transitional organ of government. Transitional to what? What eventually was envisaged would happen?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: A unified Serbian state.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, when they are stating, a few lines down, that Serbs shall not in any way participate in the referendum conducted by the SDA, to which referendum are they referring?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to the referendum on independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which was suggested by the Badinter commission of the European community and ordered by the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina in January of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So in essence, Serbs are being instructed not to participate in a democratic referendum, whether they like it or not; is that the position?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are being instructed not to participate, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the continuation of this summary on page 458, five lines down there is a discussion of the demographic forecast attributed to Dr. Karadzic. "Around 150.000 Serbs would be outside our reach, which can be handled if we have in mind 1.5 million Serbs. There would be 10 per cent Muslims here. It is necessary for us to establish control in our territories." Then the bottom of the page, Mr. Srdic: "An important argument for our transformation is the plebiscite we conducted." This refers to the Serbian plebiscite of 9, 10 November 1991: "The creation of states brings about mass emigration and resettlement, and the exchange of territories, which is imminent. This long-term process is still better than war."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So at this stage they are envisaging that the creation of their state will involve massive population resettlement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: My next observations from this document are from page 460, and they pertain to a meeting that was held the same day of the Prijedor Municipal Assembly, which at this point was still engaged in the deadlock over appointments to governmental positions. And on this page, Miskovic, one-third of the way down the page, makes the statement: "Regarding this SDA proposal for a division to have an extended coordinating body and analyse what has been proposed." Now, that refers to a rather complex proposal presented by the Prijedor SDA at this Prijedor assembly meeting, which entailed dividing portfolios in five different municipalities around Prijedor and Prijedor itself. And then two lines down, two speakers down, Pilipovic: "Our position presented before the assembly today is that the participation of Serbs in the government is disproportional. He explained in detail why the assembly was not working well." Now, this -- these two references to this SDA proposal indicate that the SDS is going to respond to this proposal, create a coordinating body, and then engage in discussions with SDA representatives, and that in fact did subsequently take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could move to the next exhibit, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 48.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a -- what's called a rough English translation. It's not an official translation, but we have put it in for official translation, and as soon as we get it back, we will submit it to the Court. But it will, I think, assist Your Honours for the moment to see what this document says in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, do you know who was appointed to coordinate with the SDA from amongst SDS officials?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the meeting of 27 December 1991, the two persons charged with creating the committee for inter-party relations were Mr. Miskovic and Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this document are minutes of a meeting which took place on the 13th of April of 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you highlight for the Judges, please, the important parts, the important elements of this meeting.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is entitled, "Prijedor SDS municipal board coordination body," and the names here are then followed by the minutes of a meeting held on 13 April 1992, in a style that is similar to those from 1991 in the book for 1991. The subject is preparation for the meeting with the SDA executive board in relation to the solution of the Prijedor problem. Mr. Babic states: "Employ tactics while speaking at the meeting. Be cool-headed, even disinterested in the division of the municipality. The position of our negotiators is defined by the Serbian Bosnia-Herzegovina," BH. Then Mr. Pilipovic states: "Insist on completing the unification of the territory of the Krajina state. Do everything in order for the entire municipality of Prijedor to join Bosnian Krajina. Possibly give local self-government to ethnic units, former municipalities." So here, in determining the negotiating position at the meeting with the SDA, the party leaders are suggesting this complete inclusion of Prijedor into the Bosnian Krajina as their ultimate objective, or one of the ultimate objectives of this negotiation. Down one speaker, Drljaca: "The president should run the show, and only the first option should be advocated." Kos at the bottom of this page says, "the existence of three options provided that the Serbian municipality of Prijedor establishes its administration organs." I note there's no break here in the original B/C/S, but there is in the English translation to the next page, where Mr. Savanovic says: "Aim at implementing Krajina laws in Prijedor municipality as well." And Mr. Miskovic says: "Take the meeting as a way of testing the grounds. Go for option number 1. The whole of Prijedor to join the Autonomous Region of Bosnian Krajina. Meanwhile, urgently establish administrative organs of the Serbian municipality of Prijedor." Then onto the next page of the translation. This is the decisions or conclusions of this meeting. Just highlight three of them. Number 2: "Miskovic and two delegates in charge of solving proposals by SUP, that is, police, secretariat of the interior, the public audit service, the bank, the court." Three of these four items, that is, the police, the public audit service and the court, were, of course, those appointments which Dr. Stakic had accused the SDA of usurping a few months earlier. Simo Drljaca and Radovan Krejic to be appointed coordinators. Point 3, "in charge of all preparations are a Serbian assembly, Stakic, Savanovic and Baltic." Number 5, "information committee to issue a statement providing information on the occurrence." This occurrence was in fact the appointment of a government for the Serbian municipality of Prijedor, which was issued on the 17th of April and reported on the 18th of April 1992 in the Banja Luka newspaper Glas.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Who was put in charge of providing that information, issuing that statement?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The issuance of the statement was charged to Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could now move to the next document, which is the meeting of the 23rd of April, which is Exhibit 47.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Does the Court have ... I think you have Exhibit 47 already. If it could be provided to the witness and the Judges. Your Honour, on that last exhibit which I referred to as 48, I made a mistake. It is in fact Prosecutor's Exhibit 49.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, this is a meeting of the 23rd of April of 1992, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could you highlight for the Judges the important elements of this meeting.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This Serbian Democratic Party of BH SDS municipal board Prijedor --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could you wait one moment. Your Honour, do you not have this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you put the document on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could a copy of it be placed on the ELMO for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, you could have my copy if --

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: You have a copy. Good. If you could read slowly, because the interpreters don't have these last two documents, I think?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One-third of the way down the page is the agenda. Point 1: "Exchange of views and an analysis of problems on the ground. President S. Miskovic reported on the situation in the municipality and talks with the SDA, which had been held in Sanski Most." These then were the negotiations that had been discussed on the 13th of April and were now completed and result in this report by Mr. Miskovic. The -- skipping down two paragraphs: "After the discussion, the board adopted the following decisions. Point 2. All units and staff in management posts shall be responsible and subordinate to the Crisis Staff in this area. 3: To reinforce the Crisis Staff according to specialty. 5: To immediately start working on the takeover, the coordination with the JNA notwithstanding." Point 6: "Put the point across that if Zeljaja (JNA) does not declare that the JNA is indeed going to protect the Serbs, the SDS will call upon all Serbian soldiers to leave the JNA and take all their weapons." So this meeting represents the decision of the SDS municipal board to move forward with a takeover with or without the support of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And if, finally --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Finally, if we could at the minutes of the 9th of May of 1992, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit SK46. Dr. Donia, this is a precis of minutes of the SDS municipal board meeting held on 9 May 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could you highlight for the Judges the important elements of this meeting, please.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reports in this meeting indicate that a takeover has taken place and that the expected progress and problems are being addressed. The first report is from Slobodan Kuruzovic. After point 2 of his presentation, he states: "Go on with the talks, observing all the proprieties, but always keep in mind the final goal. The idea is to achieve everything peacefully and without destruction." And then Milan Kovacevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What is he referring to there, Dr. Donia, do you think?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think his statement indicates that this takeover would ideally go on with no resistance from any local opposition. And insofar as possible, facilitated by negotiations. Milan Kovacevic then enumerates several points: "Replacement of staff has been carried out with all SDA leaders removed from the functions in the Municipal Assembly. The functioning of government at the level of Krajina can now be felt. Instructions and decisions are being forwarded from the top. Larger companies and institutions have separated themselves from Sarajevo." Skipping down 2: "All measures, decisions, and conclusions must be verified by the assembly." And then to the next page, page 303 of this document, in the upper right-hand corner is the ERN number. Two-thirds of the way down the page Milomir Stakic: "Here in the municipality of Prijedor, the Constitution of the Serbian Republic of BH has been implemented since 30 April 1992, along with those laws which are -- conform with the constitution." Down to the next paragraph: "The next two or three months, until the funds which are now being established actually have available money, will be the most critical period. Peace must be maintained at all costs, and the economy must be revived." And then final item of business, or two final items of business: "A committee has been established to welcome the troops coming back from the front lines." This refers to the return of the Fifth Kozara Brigade from Croatia. "It is chaired by Savanovic and has five members. Full mobilisation is compulsory and all Serbs must respond to the call-up." So this meeting indicates that a takeover has been put in place. It has resulted in the beginning of financial flows to meet urgent needs that the government of the Krajina is now beginning to administer -- have an administrative impact on the region and that SDS leaders have been removed from their positions in the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, you state, "It had an administrative impact on the region and SDS leaders have been removed from their positions in the municipal assembly."

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: SDA. Excuse me. I erred and should have said, "SDA leaders were removed."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So in a sense, in effect, basically the Muslim leadership had been removed from the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's Mr. Kovacevic's statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I've now completed my examination-in-chief. I've run two minutes over, but nevertheless, we are now at a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Dr. Donia. My understanding is that on Monday, 22 April, there will be a

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that we agreed with the Prosecution that the cross of Dr. Donia would be on Wednesday, if I understood it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I have to say, I wasn't a party to these negotiations, but we're content with Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you cross-check? What about the other witnesses that we don't run into a problem there, because until now, my understanding was that cross-examination should be the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I have to admit that I was thinking -- both the 22nd and Wednesday ring a bell, so I probably have heard both. I'm a little confused. As long as it fits with Dr. Donia's schedule, I think it actually would be better for us to have it on Wednesday, because I think the next witness, who is protected, I hope he can finish on Monday. I don't think we're going to finish with him this week. So I'd rather him finish on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would that be convenient with you, Dr. Donia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it will, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So then let's do it on Wednesday, 24. And I would appreciate if we would have the possibility then also in short go through the documents not yet translated, especially the excerpts from newspapers, in order to find out which document is really relevant for the case which has to be translated or not. I would ask the parties to be prepared to give their own assessment, then on Wednesday, after the cross, or possibly the re-examination of Dr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, your legal officer informed me that you were going to raise this. The reason that they are all incorporated within the bundle is because each of the exhibits represents a footnote in the report, and we felt, for completeness, so that the Defence is aware of all of the documents that Dr. Donia has referred to, that they all be included in the file. I realise it does impact on translation. All of these newspaper reports have to be translated. But as I stand now, I think our position would be that they should all be admitted into evidence, otherwise it's going to lead to a situation where the report, which is evidence, is not complete, because it won't have all of the documents which are footnoted in that report as exhibits. If we can think of a better solution than that, I will try for the sake of the translation department.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this understanding, because we always take into account -- we have limited resources, especially human resources, and therefore we all have to show to a certain extent self-restraint only to translate the real necessary documents and probably we can help out for example by translating the one or other sentence here in the courtroom and then we have it completed. So therefore, please be prepared to do this exercise next Wednesday as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Or another possible solution, Your Honour, might be to simply translate the relevant excerpt rather than the entire article, if it's like five lines within the article.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But this should be indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And as I said before, a possible solution could be that it would be translated. Fortunately, we have on the Bench a Judge understanding and reading this language, and I hope also the Defence counsel can point out possibly when there is another line which should be translated from their point of view, then we could proceed this way and we have not to wait for the translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What I will do, then, Your Honour, is I will get together with Dr. Donia, go through the newspaper articles, identify the parts that need translation, highlight them, then meet with Defence counsel, offer to them the parts that we propose should be translated. If they want any additions to that, we can agree that at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is this fine with the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect, no. I hesitate to say that. I don't mind the procedure, but I don't necessarily want the Office of the Prosecutor to meet with Dr. Donia and go over and further prepare him. He is called as a witness. He's under oath. It's my understanding the Rules state that he continues to be under oath until Your Honour excuses him. So I'm a little uncomfortable with that aspect of it. We reserved our right for cross-examination to try to highlight what we believe, and respectfully to Dr. Donia, some inconsistencies in how he interprets certain articles, so we hope to bring that out in our cross. If they can assist us by giving us the documents and their translation, then we'll compare it with what we think the actual the actual translation is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Couldn't it be a possible solution that you meet together, both parties, with Dr. Donia and then both of you highlight the parts you want really to have translated?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That seems acceptable to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So if essentially we all three parties - the witness, the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, we can arrange that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for your cooperation, and then hopefully we'll meet again next Wednesday, Dr. Donia. Thank you for today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one matter Defence counsel has raised. I'm going to need to have contact with Dr. Donia in order to organise this, in order to organise this meeting, and if you can just state -- I know you said yesterday you come from a civil law system, where this is not a problem. I think my learned friend comes from probably the most extreme form of the common law system where this is a problem and certainly in my system in England it's not a problem for counsel to have contact with expert witnesses. But as I say, I will need to speak with the witness in order to organise this meeting that is proposed should take place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, I have no problem with this, and I would appreciate if also the Defence takes the opportunity, for example, in preparing the cross-examination to contact the expert witness. From our point of view, there's no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I should respond. We don't mind if the Office of the Prosecutor schedules and does preliminary administrative things with the expert witnesses. What we did earlier object to is the Prosecutor's characterisation of how they want to meet, go over documents and in my view spend more time than necessary but for scheduling and administrative, we don't have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is my understanding and I believe this is really the solution that when it comes to the question of the relevance of documents, what has to be translated, please contact and have a meeting together, both parties, with Dr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I will organise that, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. The Office of the Prosecutor is prepared now to discuss issues of the deposition witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then let's proceed. As it was said already the last days, we should stick with that, what has been said in the past. You made your request, and the request is, of course, based on a former meeting earlier this year of the parties under Rule 65 ter (i), and it was our understanding that in both cases, Dr. Stakic and Momir Talic separate decisions should be taken depending on the relevance to each case. The Judges in this case have already decided that it is necessary to hear for in this case viva voce, or better, live, Witness 1, 2, 6, 8, and 9. Witness 8 on the list is already summoned to appear as a live witness in the courtroom, and what we have to discuss are the remaining witnesses, and here I would like to hear some comments from the side of the Office of the Prosecutor first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: First, I think everyone understands our position, but if I could just restate it to be clear. We filed the motion for deposition before both Chambers. In order to avoid the witnesses testifying twice in both cases, we were not proposing that these witnesses be 92 bis or submitted on a transcript. We always anticipated that they would testify live, with cross-examination. The only issue would be whether it was before a judicial officer, which we pointed out could be a Judge also, or whether it would be before the entire Chambers. And I understand Your Honour's rulings on these witnesses. First to clarify that if either Chamber would deny that motion, we would not be interested, of course, in proceeding by way of deposition, because the point was to have the witness testify only once before on both cases. And so assuming that the Courts are not going to grant the deposition on both cases, although we did not file a motion for 92 bis, taking advantage of, appreciating Your Honour's indications, we would indicate that Witness 5 and 10 we do believe would be appropriate for 92 bis, to have their testimony presented by way of 92 bis and we would offer to do so. The other witnesses we feel should testify. We are maintaining our motion regarding the videolink witnesses, that they either be taken by way of deposition or by videolink, testify before the entire Trial Chamber. When I say Witnesses 5 and 10, I'm referring to the number on our deposition motion. Actually, the Rule 65 numbers are 27 and 44.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Number 4 remains unclear, and there it was not possible to come to an assessment in the Trial Chamber because until now the references mentioned in the document, the so-called ICTY statements, were not included in this motion and they are not included in the exhibits disclosed until now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, we are hoping to call that witness live, and in fact to schedule that witness to replace the one who is unable to come -- coming up, so we're trying to arrange for that witness to be here, if not next week, then the week after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I hear the opinion of the Defence as regards Witness 5 and 10, and videolink as regards Witnesses 3 and 7, where there is a clear intention of -- I can already say now - of the Trial Chamber to hear both witnesses separately by videolink, or, if you regard it necessary, to try to hear these witnesses live. But please give your comments on the five remaining witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would first address the issue with the witnesses who would testify by the means of the videolink. I think that it's pointless and it's not too hard for the witnesses to go to the SFOR base in Banja Luka. It's probably a few kilometres from their home. So I don't think it's necessary to hold actually two trials to have those witnesses to travel two or three kilometres. So we absolutely require those witnesses to testify by the videolink in front of both Chambers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can this be agreed by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, and we appreciate especially the indication in front of both Chambers, if that can be arranged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But separately, it was your understanding; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, do two separate examinations. Perhaps we can talk about this later, but yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we have to come to a conclusion in order to know the number of witnesses, how they shall be presented, and so on, and this should be done, as indicated beforehand, today, and therefore, I had discussed this point with technicians, security, and the witness section of the Tribunal, and I heard this would not cause special problems with regard also to these two witnesses, and therefore really it should be done separately, two separate videolink hearings of both witnesses. Is that agreed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It's agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then we learn already Witness 4 would appear live in courtroom. Then what about Witness 5? The suggestion was to hear this witness under Rule 92 bis, and this indeed was a provisional opinion of the Trial Chamber as well, because it's more or less a repetition of what can be said and probably will be said by other witnesses. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If Your Honours think that it's acceptable, we agree, only we'll see if we can get the chance to cross-examine those witnesses, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes and no. I think really the parties should look into the merits and what will be expected by these witnesses beforehand, because we can't afford first to proceed in a way expecting to hear a witness under Rule 92 bis and then later on the question of cross-examination, because there can't be any kind of surprise in the future. You know beforehand what are the statements given until now, and on this basis it can be decided. Of course, we have to make use of Rule 92 bis more than beforehand, first of all to avoid repetitions. So would you agree Witness 5 to be introduced under Rule 92 bis?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I don't agree, Your Honour. I would like to cross-examine those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can you give special reasons why you need this witness for cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Your Honour, I don't have those statements with me right now, so I cannot point out specifically why, but I think that we will be able to answer this question tomorrow morning. Probably we'll need not more than five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This should be the exception. If future, I would really expect when I announce that we want to discuss points the next day, then it should be the next day. Today I want to make an exception, but in future we should all be prepared to discuss the issues on the basis of the already disclosed material.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And what about Witness 10? It was also the suggestion, both by the Trial Chamber, of course provisionally, and the Office of the Prosecutor, under 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that we have the same position, Your Honour, regarding this witness as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then we will return to Witness 5 and 10 tomorrow with your final position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and I apologise once again for not being ready for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. From the side of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I would ask the Court, if I could, to please address -- ask Your Honours to hear a little more regarding the reasons for the videolink of Witness 3. Your Honour indicated we would have not one but two separate times. I would ask that the Trial Chamber and in both cases to consider the possibility of arranging it so that the witness only comes one time, and it seems to me like it would be very technically feasible for one direct examination and then to have the cross-examinations can be separate. This is a gentleman with a severe heart problems and the reason we're asking for the videolink is to avoid him having to testify two times. Neither side, neither Defence would be prejudiced. Both Trial Chambers would have the opportunity to ask questions of the witness. We would have two completely separate cross-examinations. We would just like to arrange it so that he testifies on one day, one direct examination, and then undergoes two separate cross-examinations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Of course, having read the health certificates, I understand your point, but on the other hand, it's a probably important witness, and we are more than hesitant to confuse both cases. There is a different approach. We discuss individual criminal responsibility, and therefore we would ask the Office of the Prosecutor to realise the best possible solution. Probably it may be that you ask this witness only to come once to this videolink station and then at the same day a hearing in both cases. This is a question of the arrangement of the presentation of the Prosecutor's case, and I'll leave it to you, but both Chambers agreed already that there should -- it's mandatory to have a separate hearing. So therefore, please be prepared to do so. And once again, to avoid any kind of confusion, this is also true as regards Witness 6. No doubt that Witness 6, at least in the case against Dr. Stakic, has to be heard separately and live in courtroom. So to finalise, it should not be forgotten that you please prepare us with and give us the necessary ICTY statements not yet included in the documents as regards Witness 4. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It's understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we can -- we'll only come back in the beginning of the hearing of tomorrow to Witnesses 5 and 10, and then there will be the final ruling. May we now turn to the witness of today, and it still remains as it is, protected witness number, not as it was indicated, 28, but 39; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the protection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It's closed session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 19th day of April, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.50 p.m.,
